subject: Private deployment addendum — operator attestation & evidence deposit
messages:
From: Carol Lewis <carol.lewis@acmehealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment addendum — operator attestations and evidence deposit

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Procurement and legal here at Acme want to nail down the addendum language for the private deployment (VPC/on‑prem) we're contracting for. Two specific asks came up in our review of your Order Form and the MSA redlines:

1) Evidence deposit: we'd like a binding mechanism that allows Acme to validate application continuity in a catastrophic event. Our preference is a "sealed snapshot deposit" held with a neutral third party or notarized custodian — accessible only upon mutually‑agreed trigger events (termination, insolvency, or subpoena). We do not want regular access, only a forensics‑style recovery pathway.

2) Operator attestations / witness: because this is an airgapped clinical environment, our compliance team is asking for vendor attestation that operator access will be limited and that any operator activity during a witness event will be logged and notarized by a third‑party (for example, an independent forensic lab or notary).

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a sealed snapshot + third‑party witness as an alternative to a full code escrow? If so, please provide proposed addendum language and an outline of evidentiary artifacts you can provide (checksums, signed manifests, witness logs, access timestamps). I've attached our redline (Acme_MSAs_Redline_v2.pdf) and a draft addendum (Private_Deploy_Addendum_v1.docx).

Timeline: procurement needs the agreed terms by COB Nov 24 to make the Q4 procurement cycle. Please advise if that's feasible.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

—Carol
Carol Lewis
Sr. Director, Procurement
Acme Health
Attachment: Acme_MSAs_Redline_v2.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: Private_Deploy_Addendum_v1.docx (docx)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Carol Lewis <carol.lewis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment addendum — operator attestations & evidence deposit

Carol — thanks for the clear framing and the attachments.

Short answer: yes, we can accept a sealed snapshot + third‑party witness model as an alternative to traditional source code escrow, provided the scope and access conditions are well scoped in the addendum.

High‑level options we typically offer (we can pick one as the starting point):

• Sealed snapshot deposit: Redwood will create an encrypted filesystem snapshot (runtime image + configuration manifests + deterministic checksums) and deposit it with a mutually approved neutral custodian. Access to the deposit requires a two‑party trigger (Acme request + Redwood confirmation) or a contractually defined unilateral trigger (bankruptcy/insolvency). The custody agreement defines release conditions and notarized transfer procedure.

• Witnessed recovery (preferred for clinical customers): instead of releasing a full image to the customer, an independent third‑party (forensic lab) executes a recovery verification in a controlled environment and produces a notarized evidence package (hashes, runbook outputs, signed witness log). This avoids routine handover of images and limits data exposure.

• Operator‑limited access with time‑boxed test window: for audit or continuity tests, Redwood can provision an operator‑led run under strict monitoring; logs and a signed report are produced and the environment is rolled back. We can include SLA credits for any unscheduled extended operator access (open for negotiation).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Laura (Legal) and Rishi (Onboarding) review Acme's redlines and propose markups for the addendum language.
2) We'll produce a draft addendum (legal + operational exhibits) and a short evidence matrix (what artifacts we can provide and their formats).
3) Schedule a 30‑minute sync next week with Acme legal + compliance if needed.

Target: we can get a Redwood draft by EOD Nov 20 and turn around redlines fast enough for your Nov 24 procurement cutoff if we have the DocuSign/operator points nailed down.

If that timeline is tight, tell us which items you must close by Nov 24 and which can be finalised post‑signature.

—Chloe Martin
Senior Manager, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Carol Lewis <carol.lewis@acmehealth.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:01:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood proposed addendum — initial markups and compromise language

Carol / Chloe,

I reviewed Acme's redline and Chloe's options. Attached is a clean markup containing compromise language we often use for regulated customers. Key points summarised:

• License scope: runtime execution only; no assignment of model weights or rights to create derivatives beyond customer's use within its environment. We will not convey source code, model internals, or training artifacts.

• Evidence deposit: Redwood proposes a sealed snapshot deposit model with the following guards: encrypted deposit stored with an agreed custodian; release requires a written trigger event (listed in section 3); release procedure includes a notarized handoff and chain‑of‑custody report.

• Witness and forensic verification: Redwood will permit a mutually‑selected independent forensic lab to witness a recovery verification. The lab will produce a signed attestations package (hashes, verification logs, access timestamps). Redwood will not provide operator shell access to Acme outside controlled witness events.

• Audit windows and notice: propose a 90‑day advance notice for routine audits; for emergency triggers (insolvency, subpoena) notice is as‑soon‑as‑practical but release still subject to the custodian's release process.

• SLA credits: we are open to limited SLA credit for operator access events that materially exceed agreed durations — propose a capped credit formula (§6.2), to be negotiated in the order form.

I attached a draft mark‑up: Redwood_Proposed_Addendum_markups.docx. A few technical clarifications we need from Acme compliance:
- Are you ok with the 90‑day routine audit notice? If not, what notice window do you need and why?
- For the witness party, do you have a preferred vendor (forensic lab)? If not, we can share a short list.

If you accept the high‑level compromise we can produce a tracked‑change addendum for signature within two business days.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Addendum_markups.docx (docx)
From: Carol Lewis <carol.lewis@acmehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed addendum — initial markups and compromise language

Laura / Chloe — thanks for the quick turn.

High‑level: Acme can accept the sealed snapshot + forensic witness compromise, subject to two edits:

1) Routine audit notice: reduce to 30‑days (instead of 90) for operational compliance checks — our internal policy requires a shorter window to rotate local retention controls.
2) Emergency trigger: add a unilateral path for Acme to request a custody verification within 10 business days if there is a material security incident affecting our environment.

Additionally, procurement requests that any SLA credit formula be visible in the Order Form (we cannot accept a 'to be negotiated' placeholder for procurement signoff). If you can provide a capped formula we will be able to proceed to signature.

Can you produce a tracked addendum with those two edits and a DocuSign packet by EOD Nov 20? If so procurement will be able to route for approvals and hit the Nov 24 deadline.

If easier I'll jump on a 20‑minute call this afternoon — I can be available at 3pm PT.

Thanks,
—Carol
